source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 7. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

title.en: The iqamah: the prayer is starting

learn.en: The iqāmah is the second call. It is said just before the prayer begins. It means: “Stand up — the prayer is starting now!”
learn.title: Stand up!

learn.en: When you hear it, join the jamāʿah (the group), stand in straight rows and face the qiblah.
learn.title: Straight rows

learn.en: Its special phrase, said twice, is: “The prayer has begun.”
learn.title: The special phrase

learn.en: Bilal was told to say the adhan in pairs and the iqāmah once each — except “qad qāmati ṣ-ṣalāh”. (Bukhari 605)
learn.title: Pairs and singles

learn.en: The adhan calls people to come; the iqāmah tells them to stand. Even when praying alone, you may say the iqāmah quietly.
learn.title: Adhan or iqamah?

quiz.en: True or false? The adhan phrases are mostly in pairs and the iqāmah phrases mostly single.
True or false? When we hear the iqāmah, we stand in straight rows.

move.en: Stand in a straight row, shoulder to shoulder!

think.q: What is the difference between the adhan and the iqamah?
think.a: The adhan calls people to come when the time begins; the iqamah tells them to stand because the prayer is starting.

parents.summary: The iqāmah is the short second call before prayer. Its special phrase is “qad qāmati ṣ-ṣalāh”. We stand in straight rows facing the qiblah.
parents.tip: At home, let your child say the iqamah before you pray together.
